title: Size bound for tree unrolling
statement: Let $F$ be a Boolean layered circuit with input type $	ext{Fin }n$, and assign an AND-or-OR flag to each non-input node. Suppose every gate has finite arity, and for some natural number $k$ every gate's arity is at most $k$. For every $m<	ext{depth}(F)+1$ and every node $v$ at layer $m$, the tree obtained by recursively unrolling $v$ has size at most $(k+1)^m$.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a Boolean layered circuit with input type $	ext{Fin }n$
An AND-or-OR flag is specified for each gate's output node
There is a natural number $k$ bounding every gate's arity
replaced:
Let $F$ be a Boolean feedforward circuit from the inputs $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$ to an output
type, in which every gate has finitely many input wires, and suppose $k \in \bbn$ bounds
these arities, so that each gate has at most $k$ input wires. Then for every layer $m
\le \mathrm{depth}(F)$ and every node $v$ of layer $m$, the tree-unrolling of $v$ is a
Boolean circuit of size at most $(k+1)^m$.
